rationale: Towers is a tiny (1471 text bytes, 13 functions) recursion- and call-intensive Stanford benchmark, so the table leans on low-cost, high-diversity passes while damping cost-dominant ones: SUB and SPLIT get high diversity weights and near-minimal runtime/size/risk weights so they apply broadly and act as enablers for later transforms; FLA carries the highest SecurityGain weight since flattening the recursive Towers/Move/tower control flow yields the largest analysis deterrence per byte in such a small binary, with a moderate RuntimeCost weight keeping it off the hottest leaf functions (Push/Pop); BCF is the main size offender and its SizeCost weight is the highest in the table so it concentrates only on the largest functions (Towers, Init, Move) rather than the whole program; IBR is favored for its strong diversity and opaque-predicate synergy with FLA at moderate cost; ICALL is kept at a middling RuntimeCost weight because the program's call volume is high (recursive Push/Pop/Move chains) and indirect-call dispatch overhead would compound there, while still disrupting static call-graph recovery; IGV is included at neutral weights since the benchmark has few globals, letting feature matching decide its sparse application; all CorrectnessRisk weights stay low-to-moderate to preserve semantics of the mutually recursive structure, keeping overall runtime and size growth acceptable for a timed benchmark.
